title: Non-blocking findings from frontend-close-position-dialog's review (PR #261)
description: Non-blocking findings from pr-reviewer's review of PR #261 (frontend-close-position-dialog), tracked here per CLAUDE.md's autonomous-pipeline rule so they aren't lost once that PR merges. Both are minor reuse/style items in ClosePositionDialog.tsx and its test, distinct from the review's blocking finding (a stale/invisible close-position error after a backdrop-cancel-while-pending), which was returned to the task itself for a real fix rather than tracked here.

checklist.step: `isPositiveFinite` in `frontend/src/features/portfolio/components/ClosePositionDialog.tsx` (around line 79) is a verbatim copy of the identical helper already defined in `frontend/src/features/portfolio/components/AddPositionDialog.tsx` (around line 48) -- extract it to a shared location (e.g. a small validation utility module) so a future change to the rule (e.g. allowing zero, or adding a max) doesn't have to be made in two places and risk drifting out of sync.

Minor indentation inconsistency in `frontend/src/features/portfolio/components/ClosePositionDialog.test.tsx`: the `error={null}` prop is over-indented by 2 extra spaces relative to its sibling props on both occurrences (around lines 44 and 196). Cosmetic only (eslint/prettier didn't flag it), but worth a quick fix for consistency.

PR #261 round-2 review (a `code-review` skill pass) flagged that `PositionsTable`'s single shared `useDeletePosition()` instance means a second `mutate()` call detaches TanStack Query's mutation observer from whatever close attempt the first call was still tracking -- in isolation this reads as a way a second, different position's close (confirmed before the first settles) could orphan the first's eventual error entirely (neither the in-dialog error nor the page-level banner would ever show it). The reviewer verified empirically (two positions with independently-controlled held DELETE responses in a real browser) that this is *not* currently reachable through the UI: `ClosePositionDialog`'s Confirm button receives `isPending` unscoped from the shared mutation, so any open dialog's Confirm button is disabled table-wide while *any* close is in flight, not just for its own row -- a second dialog cannot actually be confirmed until the first settles. This safety is an incidental side effect of `isPending` being passed unscoped rather than a deliberately documented/tested invariant, so a future change (e.g. scoping `isPending` per-row for better UX, since right now opening an unrelated position's dialog while another closes shows its Confirm button confusingly already in a loading state) could silently reintroduce the orphaned-error bug with nothing to catch it. Add an explicit regression test asserting a second position's dialog Confirm button stays disabled while a different position's close is still pending, and a doc-comment note on `PositionsTable`'s existing doc comment explaining *why* overlapping closes can't happen (not just asserting that they don't), so `belongsToOpenDialog`'s own 'never invisible' claim is backed by a verified mechanism rather than an implicit one.

decisions.decision: Extracted `isPositiveFinite` into a new `frontend/src/utils/validation.ts` module (with its own `validation.test.ts` unit test) rather than e.g. a `features/portfolio`-local shared file, and updated both `AddPositionDialog.tsx` and `ClosePositionDialog.tsx` to import it from there.
decisions.rationale: The existing `frontend/src/utils/` directory already holds exactly this kind of small, dependency-free, cross-feature helper (e.g. `signColor.ts`, extracted from two components the same way per frontend-trade-journal-followups) -- `isPositiveFinite` has no portfolio-specific meaning of its own (it's a generic numeric-validation predicate) and both call sites already import other things from `../../../utils/format`, so `utils/` is the established, discoverable home for it rather than introducing a new features/portfolio-scoped validation file for a single function that isn't domain-specific to portfolios at all.

decisions.decision: Placed the new regression test (second position's dialog Confirm button disabled while a different position's close is pending) in `PositionsTable.test.tsx` rather than `ClosePositionDialog.test.tsx`, and left an unresolved side detail out of its assertions: after the test lets the first (AAPL) DELETE settle so it doesn't leak into a later test, it does not assert on `ClosePositionDialog`'s post-resolve state (e.g. that the button re-enables), only on a local `deleteSettled` flag.
decisions.rationale: The invariant under test is inherently about two dialogs sharing one `PositionsTable`-owned `useDeletePosition()` mutation instance -- `ClosePositionDialog` itself takes `isPending` as a prop and has no opinion on where it comes from, so the interesting behavior (opening a second position's dialog while the first's mutate() is still in flight) can only be exercised at the `PositionsTable` level, matching where the existing analogous tests (the double-click-race guard test, the delayed-failure-misattribution test) already live. Separately, `handleConfirmClose`'s per-call `onSuccess: () => setPendingDelete(null)` callback is bound to whichever position's `mutate()` call it was given to, not to whatever `pendingDelete` currently holds when it later fires -- so if AAPL's held DELETE is resolved while ZZZZ's dialog is what's now open, AAPL's own onSuccess still fires and clears `pendingDelete`, closing ZZZZ's dialog out from under it. That's a real, pre-existing, separate latent quirk of `PositionsTable.tsx` (not something this task's 3 checklist items call for fixing, and not the orphaned-error bug this checklist item's own test is verifying protection against), so the test deliberately doesn't assert on the dialog's state after resolving the held DELETE -- it only confirms the request itself settled, without asserting anything that would depend on which of the two behaviors is 'correct' here. Not filed as a separate followup task since it's a narrow, latent edge case with no `depends_on` chain of its own review flagging it yet; if a future reviewer wants it tracked, the natural home is a new `<id>-followups` entry against this task or `frontend-close-position-dialog`.

comments.summary: Verified `isPositiveFinite` in `frontend/src/utils/validation.ts` is byte-identical to both removed copies (diffed against `main`'s versions in `AddPositionDialog.tsx`/`ClosePositionDialog.tsx`); new `validation.test.ts` covers positive, zero, negative, NaN, and Infinity. Both dialogs' existing tests still pass with the shared import, and a repo-wide grep confirms no remaining duplicate implementation.

The new PositionsTable.test.tsx regression test genuinely exercises the shared-isPending mechanism, not a tautology: it opens a second position's (ZZZZ) dialog while a different position's (AAPL) DELETE is deliberately held pending, and asserts ZZZZ's own Confirm button is disabled. ClosePositionDialog's Confirm button has no other source of disabled/loading state (only `loading={isPending}`, no form-validation-driven disable), so this correctly isolates the invariant the doc comment describes rather than incidentally passing for an unrelated reason.

Independently assessed the flagged-but-unfixed `pendingDelete` quirk in `handleConfirmClose`: it is real and reachable (open A's dialog, confirm, backdrop-dismiss while pending, open B's dialog for a different position, then A's held DELETE resolves -- A's per-call `onSuccess` unconditionally clears `pendingDelete`, closing B's dialog out from under the user right as its Confirm button would have become clickable, silently discarding whatever the user had entered for B). Confirmed via `git diff` that `handleConfirmClose` itself is untouched by this PR (pre-existing on `main`), so it's correctly out of scope for this PR's 3 checklist items rather than something that should have blocked or been fixed here. Filed as a tracked followup per CLAUDE.md's autonomous-pipeline rule: docs/tasks/frontend-close-position-dialog-followups-followups.json.

No interactive Playwright MCP browser tool was available in this review session, so step 9's exploratory walkthrough couldn't be performed tool-call by tool-call. Mitigated by: (a) `git diff` confirms zero production-behavior change in this PR (the extraction is byte-identical, the doc comment adds no logic, the only new runtime-reachable surface is the already-covered regression test), (b) the full persisted e2e suite (`make e2e`, 22/22 specs including `portfolio.spec.ts`'s add/close-position flow) passed against a real browser + real backend, and (c) the new regression test itself drives real user-event clicks/dialog interactions via Testing Library, closely mirroring the actual browser flow. Given the change's near-zero behavioral surface, this is judged sufficient in lieu of a live exploratory pass, but noting the limitation explicitly per this review's own instructions rather than silently omitting it.

Frontend: vitest 831/831 passed, coverage 99.76%/99.31%/99.78%/99.82% (statements/branches/functions/lines), well above the 90% gate. Static analysis clean on both sides (ruff, mypy, eslint, tsc, profit-target-wording guard). Background `code-review` skill pass (effort: high) independently found zero findings, consistent with this review's own manual diff inspection. `validate_tasks.py` reports no board violations. No API/schema changes, so no OpenAPI snapshot check applies. No new module/dependency/layer, so architecture-review wasn't separately loaded (the extraction target, frontend/src/utils/, is an existing, already-established location per the task's own decisions entry and matches the signColor.ts precedent). No new/substantially-changed frontend components (only two existing feature dialogs' import lines and a table's doc comment changed), so the common/-vs-feature placement check in step 7a doesn't add anything beyond confirming the new validation.ts utility (not a component) is correctly domain-agnostic and correctly placed in utils/ rather than a feature folder. One non-blocking finding filed as a followup task (see comments above); no blocking findings.

pr_decision.notes: Independently re-ran everything: frontend vitest 831/831 passed with coverage 99.76%/99.31%/99.78%/99.82% (statements/branches/functions/lines) matching pr-reviewer exactly; backend pytest 1203/1203 passed at 100% coverage; eslint and tsc -b both clean; validate_tasks.py clean. Diffed `isPositiveFinite` extraction against both removed copies -- byte-identical logic, only import sites changed. Confirmed the new PositionsTable.test.tsx regression test (line ~255) is meaningful, not tautological: it holds one position's DELETE pending, opens a second position's dialog, and asserts its Confirm button is disabled via the shared unscoped `isPending`, matching the mechanism the new doc comment describes. Verified via `git diff origin/main...HEAD -- PositionsTable.tsx` that `handleConfirmClose` itself is untouched by this PR (only appears inside new doc-comment prose), confirming pr-reviewer's out-of-scope call for the follow-up bug was correct; also confirmed docs/tasks/frontend-close-position-dialog-followups-followups.json was filed correctly with depends_on this task.
